- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.4), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for risk reversal.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3 periods.  
- Model consistently underestimates mean-reversion zones; if 3 consecutive days show downward trend, add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to next forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model overfits short-term volatility; smooth 30d forecast by averaging last 7–10 days’ prices unless sentiment strongly diverges.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.6, -0.4, +0.6), model fails to capture sentiment momentum; adjust forecast to align with sentiment swing direction.
